input.description: Restructure the contribution around an inference-isolating factorial design, executed in explicit stages so no claim depends on an unverified component. Stage 1 (primary): one base model and one KG, arms with matched example counts, matched total supervision tokens, matched prompt template and matched optimization steps — (A) isolated triple/path; (B) target + passage-derived context triples; (C) target + an equal-length set of irrelevant/random triples; (D) target + relevance-selected context triples at the same token count as B; primary contrast B vs. C, with A vs. C as the extra-context manipulation check and a no-fine-tuning LLM reference. Stage 2 (conditional): only if Stage 1 shows a context effect, add error-type attribution and targeted repair (M003) as an ablation on top of the frozen Stage-1 winner, reporting per-type repair rates. Stage 3 (deferred, separately reported): the lower-hop RL extension, evaluated only if Stage 1 or 2 leaves a hop-transfer gap that supervised fine-tuning on lower-hop data does not close. Each stage is reported as its own result, so a null Stage 1 does not invalidate the diagnostic output of Stage 2.
input.expected_benefit: Makes every claim attributable and removes the pipeline confound identified in U007: no single published claim depends on the repair loop or the RL stage, and each component's contribution is isolated by construction. It also guarantees a useful outcome even if the primary hypothesis fails (a clean matched-budget negative result plus an error-type diagnostic).
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Stage 1 alone requires careful construction of the irrelevant-triple arm (length- and structure-matched but semantically unrelated), token accounting across arms, and multiple seeds; Stages 2-3 add perturbation harnesses and RL training but are conditional, so the cost is incurred only if earlier stages justify it.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: No new model components are needed for Stage 1 beyond an isolated-triple baseline that already exists; the work is mainly data construction and budget accounting. Stages 2-3 reuse already-proposed components (M003 and RL) and are gated on Stage-1 outcomes.
input.main_risk: The irrelevant-triple control may itself change behaviour (e.g. teach 'ignore context'), and exact token matching can force unnatural truncation. Gating Stage 2 on Stage 1 means the repair and RL contributions may never be tested if the context effect is null, which must be presented as a scope decision rather than a hidden omission.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged: the context family is crowded, so novelty is the matched-budget causal test with an equal-length irrelevant arm plus staged attribution in a training-time KGQA setting, not 'adding context'. A null or quantity-attributable result is itself a publishable negative finding.
required_baselines: Relevance-selected context at matched token count (arm D)
NSM-style intermediate supervision (reproduced under the same budget)
input.technical_mechanism: Keep the supervision pipeline unchanged; only vary what accompanies each target triple/path. For each target, materialise four context versions with identical serialization and token counts. Enforce matched example counts and matched total supervision tokens by truncating or padding the context field (padding drawn from the irrelevant pool for arm C), and log exact token counts per arm. Run Stage 1 to completion first; only if the primary contrast is positive, freeze that configuration and layer error-type-attributed repair (Stage 2), then the lower-hop RL extension (Stage 3). Analyse Stage 1 as a within-example paired comparison across arms plus a between-seed variance estimate.
input.title: Make the matched-budget context-relevance ablation the primary experiment, executed in gated stages
input.why_differs: DrKGC warns about long-context noise but treats subgraph compactness as a design choice with no matched control; SG-RAG MOT varies context scope without a no-context or equal-length-irrelevant arm; the IKG/KGSweetSpot study compares triple vs. path representations and relevance filtering only in prompts for multiple-choice QA, with no training and no budget matching. Unlike the original bundled proposal, this version never tests three unverified components at once, so no reported claim depends on the repair loop or RL stage working.

input.direction: Decouple the bundled pipeline hypothesis. The primary hypothesis is now single-component and carries the contribution (under matched example counts and supervision tokens, does context *relevance* drive any multi-hop KGQA and deeper-hop transfer benefit?). The repair loop becomes a conditional second hypothesis with its own diagnostic (does a one-hop failure localize a base-fact error, and are those failures repairable?), and the lower-hop RL stage becomes a deferred third hypothesis tested only if supervised fine-tuning on lower-hop data leaves a transfer gap. Components are executed in gated stages (revised M001) and reported separately, so a null primary result does not invalidate the diagnostics, and a positive primary result is not contaminated by an unverified repair or RL stage.
input.hypothesis: Stage 1 (primary): Under matched example counts and total supervision tokens, relevance-selected co-passage context triples outperform an equal-length irrelevant-context control on multi-hop KGQA and held-out deeper-hop transfer; the isolated-triple and irrelevant-context arms do not differ beyond noise. Stage 2 (conditional): one-hop failures are predominantly caused by incorrect base facts rather than entity-linking/retrieval or composition errors, and targeted corrective examples for those failures improve accuracy without degrading unrelated questions. Stage 3 (deferred): RL on lower-hop instances improves deeper-hop transfer beyond what supervised fine-tuning on lower-hop instances already provides.
input.rationale: U007 asked whether the three-component pipeline is too confounded for a clean claim; the evidence says yes. The auxiliary components are separately precedented — intermediate supervision is NSM's contribution and RL for multi-hop KG reasoning is KG-Hopper's (C012) — while the pipeline rests on two unevidenced assumptions: that one-hop failures localize base-fact errors (C010) and that the three stages can each be ablated independently under a fixed budget (C011). The stage-1 confound is itself component-specific and unresolved: the context arm necessarily adds tokens, and the literature disagrees on whether extra context helps or injects noise (C003 vs. C004, C014), while newly retrieved evidence shows imprecise KG context can fall below the no-context baseline (C015) and that context use is trainable (C018), so the relevance question is both sharper and more informative than the bundled claim. Decoupling the hypothesis makes each claim attributable and preserves a clean negative-result path; it also reduces the feasibility burden flagged in U011 because only Stage 1 must be fully resourced up front. This is worth doing next because it converts an un-attributable bundle into one causally testable claim with pre-registered controls.

input.resolution: Resolved in favour of scoping down. The evidence shows the pipeline cannot support a single clean claim: the repair loop depends on the unevidenced locality assumption that one-hop failures localize bad base facts (C010), the three stages are assumed independently ablatable without evidence (C011), and both auxiliary components are separately precedented in prior work — intermediate supervision (NSM) and RL for multi-hop KG reasoning (KG-Hopper) — so the bundled contribution adds attribution risk without adding novelty (C012). Meanwhile the context-relevance question is separately testable and has a clean negative-result path (C014, C015, C019). Enacted by direction D001 and the revised M001: a gated, staged protocol with a single primary hypothesis (Stage 1: does context relevance beat an equal-length irrelevant control under matched budgets?), a conditional repair hypothesis (Stage 2, only if one-hop failures are shown to localize base-fact errors), and a deferred RL hypothesis (Stage 3, only if supervised lower-hop training leaves a transfer gap).

input.confidence_basis: Follows directly from the staged scoping decision (D001/D002, revised M001); the provenance-dataset requirement is evidenced (C001, C013) but no candidate dataset has yet been verified in the retrieved literature.
input.resolution: Partially resolved by scoping: because only the Stage-1 context-relevance comparison must be fully resourced up front (revised M001), the compute burden drops from a three-stage pipeline to a four-arm factorial fine-tuning study, with repair and RL gated on Stage-1 outcomes. The remaining feasibility question is narrower and concrete: does a provenance-bearing, text-grounded KG with a usable train/dev/test split and a defensible hop-stratified split exist, or must one be built? That is now a data-availability verification task rather than a pipeline-budget question.

input.description: The deferred Stage-3 RL component is precedented as a strong performer (KG-Hopper reports a 7B RL-trained model outperforming much larger multi-step systems up to 70B on eight KG reasoning benchmarks), which raises the possibility that any deeper-hop transfer gain will come from the RL stage rather than from context supervision, or conversely that RL is unnecessary because supervised training on lower-hop instances already transfers. Which stage actually drives transfer is untested.
input.question: Does the held-out deeper-hop transfer claim require RL on lower-hop instances (KG-Hopper-style), or does supervised fine-tuning on lower-hop instances with context-enriched supervision already transfer, making the RL stage unnecessary?
input.rationale: Determines whether the deferred RL stage is a necessary part of the investigation or an avoidable expense and confound; if supervised lower-hop training transfers, the pipeline simplifies to a single training method.

input.description: Restructure the contribution around an inference-isolating factorial design, executed in explicit stages so no claim depends on an unverified component. Stage 1 (primary): one base model and one KG, arms with matched example counts, matched total supervision tokens, matched prompt template and matched optimization steps — (A) isolated triple/path; (B) target + passage-derived context triples; (C) target + an equal-length set of irrelevant/random triples; (D) target + relevance-selected context triples at the same token count as B; primary contrast B vs. C, with A vs. C as the extra-context manipulation check and a no-fine-tuning LLM reference. Stage 2 (conditional): only if Stage 1 shows a context effect, add error-type attribution and targeted repair (M003) as an ablation on top of the frozen Stage-1 winner, reporting per-type repair rates. Stage 3 (deferred, separately reported): the lower-hop RL extension, evaluated only if Stage 1 or 2 leaves a hop-transfer gap that supervised fine-tuning on lower-hop data does not close. Each stage is reported as its own result, so a null Stage 1 does not invalidate the diagnostic output of Stage 2.
input.expected_benefit: Makes every claim attributable and removes the pipeline confound identified in U007: no single published claim depends on the repair loop or the RL stage, and each component's contribution is isolated by construction. It also guarantees a useful outcome even if the primary hypothesis fails (a clean matched-budget negative result plus an error-type diagnostic).
input.experimental_difficulty_basis: Stage 1 alone requires careful construction of the irrelevant-triple arm (length- and structure-matched but semantically unrelated), token accounting across arms, and multiple seeds; Stages 2-3 add perturbation harnesses and RL training but are conditional, so the cost is incurred only if earlier stages justify it.
input.implementation_difficulty_basis: No new model components are needed for Stage 1 beyond an isolated-triple baseline that already exists; the work is mainly data construction and budget accounting. Stages 2-3 reuse already-proposed components (M003 and RL) and are gated on Stage-1 outcomes.
input.main_risk: The irrelevant-triple control may itself change behaviour (e.g. teach 'ignore context'), and exact token matching can force unnatural truncation. Gating Stage 2 on Stage 1 means the repair and RL contributions may never be tested if the context effect is null, which must be presented as a scope decision rather than a hidden omission.
input.potential_novelty: Hedged: the context family is crowded, so novelty is the matched-budget causal test with an equal-length irrelevant arm plus staged attribution in a training-time KGQA setting, not 'adding context'. A null or quantity-attributable result is itself a publishable negative finding.
required_baselines: Relevance-selected context at matched token count (arm D)
NSM-style intermediate supervision (reproduced under the same budget)
input.technical_mechanism: Keep the supervision pipeline unchanged; only vary what accompanies each target triple/path. For each target, materialise four context versions with identical serialization and token counts. Enforce matched example counts and matched total supervision tokens by truncating or padding the context field (padding drawn from the irrelevant pool for arm C), and log exact token counts per arm. Run Stage 1 to completion first; only if the primary contrast is positive, freeze that configuration and layer error-type-attributed repair (Stage 2), then the lower-hop RL extension (Stage 3). Analyse Stage 1 as a within-example paired comparison across arms plus a between-seed variance estimate.
input.title: Make the matched-budget context-relevance ablation the primary experiment, executed in gated stages
input.why_differs: DrKGC warns about long-context noise but treats subgraph compactness as a design choice with no matched control; SG-RAG MOT varies context scope without a no-context or equal-length-irrelevant arm; the IKG/KGSweetSpot study compares triple vs. path representations and relevance filtering only in prompts for multiple-choice QA, with no training and no budget matching. Unlike the original bundled proposal, this version never tests three unverified components at once, so no reported claim depends on the repair loop or RL stage working.
